questions.prompt: Your team leader asks what you will do tomorrow morning. Tell me one thing you will write or make — an email, an action plan, an idea for your team. Keep it short.

questions.prompt: Tell me about an old friend or an old teacher you remember. Two short sentences are enough.

instruction.sentence_length: short single-clause sentences, about 5-8 words, patterns like 'I need to...' or 'I ate...'; add a second short sentence only when the learner sounds comfortable
instruction.hint_timing: let the learner finish first, then hint only after one full try
contexts: a short check-in with a team leader
talking about a person you remember

level.reason: 짧은 일상 문장은 만들지만 관사와 발음이 아직 불안정해서 A2에서 더 다져야 해요.

notes: Articles appear when the phrase is memorized ('a meeting', 'a joke' after correction) but disappear with longer noun phrases like 'project architecture meeting'.
'an' before vowel sounds is pronounced like 'a', so 'an action plan' loses the /n/ link — worth drilling with an+vowel nouns.
Learner often produces answers in fragments across separate turns; encourage one complete short sentence per turn.
